chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating lentils softens the heart and increases weeping.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of eating lentils according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi, tracing back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quoting Imam Ali (AS), highlights the spiritual efficacy of lentils in softening the heart and inducing tears, a physical manifestation of khushu' (humility) and repentance. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often linked to the concept of 'raqiqat al-qalb' (softness of the heart), where simple foods are believed to facilitate spiritual receptivity and emotional connection with the Divine. The emphasis on tears underscores the importance of emotional sincerity in worship, a theme frequently discussed in Tafsir and Hadith commentaries regarding the effects of diet on the soul.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the lentils softens the heat and frequents the tears’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,
’Eating lintels softens the heart and increases tears.’”
